statement_record.book: Given F : C -> E and K : C -> D, a left Kan extension of F along K is a functor Lan_K F : D -> E with eta : F => (Lan_K F) . K such that every pair (G : D -> E, gamma : F => G K) factors uniquely through eta as gamma = (alpha K) . eta; dually a right Kan extension is Ran_K F : D -> E with epsilon : (Ran_K F) . K => F through which every delta : G K => F factors uniquely. K need not be a subcategory inclusion.
statement_record.intree: Class LocalLeftKan (X : A ⟶ C) := { LocalLan : B ⟶ C; lan_transform : X ⟹ LocalLan ◯ F; ump_lan (M : B ⟶ C) (ε : X ⟹ M ◯ F) : ∃! δ, ε ≈ δ ⊲ F ∙ lan_transform; }  (and the dual LocalRightKan with ump_ran (M) (μ : M ◯ F ⟹ X) : ∃! δ, μ ≈ ran_transform ∙ δ ⊲ F)

statement_record.book: Fix K : C -> D and E. IF the left (resp. right) Kan extension along K of EVERY F : C -> E exists, THEN these assignments define a left (resp. right) adjoint to the restriction functor K^* : E^D -> E^C, i.e. Lan_K -| K^* -| Ran_K, and the Kan extension unit/counit are the components of the adjunction unit/counit. CONVERSELY (following paragraph, by uniqueness of adjoints), objects in the image of any left or right adjoint to a precomposition functor ARE Kan extensions.
statement_record.intree: Class LeftKan := { Lan : [A, C] ⟶ [B, C]; lan_adjoint : Lan ⊣ Induced } / Class RightKan := { Ran; ran_adjoint : Induced ⊣ Ran }, plus LeftKan_to_LocalLeftKan {R : LeftKan} (X : A ⟶ C) : LocalLeftKan X := {| LocalLan := Lan X; lan_transform := to (adj lan_adjoint X (Lan X)) nat_id |} and dually RightKan_to_LocalRightKan.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the CONVERSE direction is proved. The library DEFINES the global Kan extension to be an adjoint of Induced (so 'Lan_K ⊣ K^*' is a definition here, not a theorem), and then proves the converse half of Prop 6.1.6 — that each object in the image of such an adjoint, with the adjunction transpose of the identity as its unit/counit, satisfies the local Kan-extension universal property. Riehl's actual forward implication (all local extensions exist ⇒ they assemble into an adjoint) is not derived. The in-tree restriction functor Induced is the honest K^* = (− ◯ K) with fmap the whiskering, so the setting matches.

gap: The forward direction of Proposition 6.1.6 is missing: there is no theorem of the form `(∀ X : A ⟶ C, LocalLeftKan X) → LeftKan F` (nor its dual `(∀ X, LocalRightKan X) → RightKan F`). Nothing in the tree turns a family of local Kan extensions into the global adjoint. The generic machinery for exactly this exists and is unused here — Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:214 `Definition AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows (H : forall c : C, UniversalArrow c U) : @Adjunction _ _ (LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows H) U` (with `Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); ... }` at line 127) — but it is never instantiated at U := Induced, and no lemma identifies `LocalLeftKan X` with `UniversalArrow X Induced`. Consequently the accompanying claim that the Kan-extension unit IS the component of the adjunction unit is only available in the converse direction (as the definition of lan_transform in LeftKan_to_LocalLeftKan), not as a theorem about an assembled adjoint.
